items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' — the call opened 'Good afternoon this is Lucas with Einstein moving, how can I help you?' and went straight into profile building. The closest thing to a roadmap came ten minutes in ('before I break down the pricing structure and how everything works'), which is a transition, not an agenda. The customer never knew the call would take 15 minutes or what the sequence would be.
Never asked 'how are you today?' or any warm-up — first substantive words after the greeting were 'have you already submitted something online?'

Meet Your Mover never mentioned. This is the cheapest available differentiator on a call where the customer explicitly said she is shopping ('I just got a couple of more places, I'm gonna call') and it went unused.

Packing services never offered or priced. The customer handed him the opening directly — 'I'm going to have everything packed and ready to go just wondering what certain things I may not need to pack' — and he answered the drawers question well but never said Einstein packs at the same hourly rate plus materials. A 30-35 box self-pack was left as a self-pack with no alternative quoted.
No 'pricing is super simple' opener — went straight to 'Sweet here with our San antonio branch we do have an hourly rate of a $96 per mover per hour.'

Access concerns never probed at either end: no question about parking or truck access at a first-floor unit in a large apartment complex, and no question about gate codes, HOA, or construction-road access at a brand-new build in a community whose street doesn't yet exist in the system. On a new-construction delivery this is the highest-risk unasked question on the call.

Walk distance never asked or priced into the estimate — he told her there are no 'long walk fees' but never established how far the walk actually is, which is the single biggest time variable in an apartment load-out.
Special considerations (narrow hallways, tight turns, elevator) and additional rooms (garage, patio/balcony, storage closet) never asked at the apartment.

Truck count never stated. The customer had to ask for the crew size herself — 'And then, I'm assuming two movers.' Trucks were named only in the inclusions list ('the trucks, the taxes the insurance'), never as 'two movers and one truck for your job.'
Traffic never named as a variable despite a 45-minute cross-town drive on an 8:30-9:00am start, and no equivalents/reference framing (school bus, etc.) used to make the 6-hour estimate concrete.

Save Your Ass speech never actually delivered. The whole prep pitch was compressed into one trailing sentence — 'the more prepared you are and the more ready you are, the faster we can be and the less money you spend at the end of the day' — with no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, photos off walls), no 'take a carload' tip, and no 'does that make sense?' close. The drawers coaching was good but it was reactive to her question, not the prep speech.

Email handoff explained but not framed: no mention of the bolded key details at the top of the email and no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask. He said 'all you have to do is reply to the email' — that was reply-to-book, not reply-to-verify, on a job whose destination address is only in the notes and could easily be wrong.
Hours of operation never given — 'just give us a quick call back' with no window attached.
Customer's name never used once in conversation. 'Taylor' appears in the transcript only when he read her email address back to her. Zero of the 3+ standard.
No Ecobox referral on a 30-35 box self-pack where the customer said 'I do kind of have a lot of stuff I accumulated' and 'now the time to' declutter.
top_strength: The estimate build was the best thing on this call and it is worth using as a teaching example. Lukas didn't just hand over a number, he showed his work: 'with a move like a two bedroom apartment move doing it locally, it takes around that four to six hour range,' then narrowed it — 'the first apartment would typically get done be like, four to five hours. I did want to add that 45 minute drive time on there and then a little bit extra time just to kind of count for the disassemble and reassembly of the four post bed. So I do have your two movers for an estimated six hours in the day which would be an estimated total of a $1,222.' That arithmetic is exactly right (6 hrs x 2 movers x $96 + $70 travel = $1,222), the padding is named rather than hidden — 'that's not set in stone, if I'm kind of being a little bit conservative' — and it is immediately paired with the downside protection: 'if they end up taking less time, you'll only pay for the time it takes on the day of.' The trip-fee handling was the trust moment of the call: rather than quoting a system number he couldn't defend, he said 'the system was putting you at $105... I reduce that travel charger down to a seventy just because we don't have that exact address we can't pin it down exactly. So I'm not gonna kinda screw you over in that sense.' The insurance explanation was also genuinely effective — the 60c/lb baseline explained through a concrete example rather than a policy recital: 'the state coverage gives you $30 to fix that with our coverage. It's a lot larger of umbrella.' And the clock section was complete: on-site walkthrough start, the minimum, 15-minute increments, and a sense-check.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: this was a shopping call and he let her leave without the two things that beat price. She said out loud 'I just got a couple of more places, I'm gonna call' — that is the cue to spend thirty seconds on Meet Your Mover, because it is the one differentiator the competitors she is about to call cannot match. The line: 'Taylor, one more thing before you shop us — a few days before the thirtieth you'll get a Meet Your Mover email with a photo and a little background on the actual guys showing up at your door, so nobody strange is walking into your new house. Ask the next company you call if they do that.' Second priority is the Save Your Ass speech, which on a 30-35 box self-pack going to a brand-new home is worth real money to her and real time to the crew. He earned the right to it and then skipped it — he needed to say 'here's how you knock an hour off this bill: box up the kids' stuff and the loose drawer items now, take the photos and mirrors off the walls, and anything small enough to fit in your car, take a carload over yourself before we get there. Does that make sense?' Instead the prep idea got one trailing sentence and the customer never got a concrete action list. Third, use her name — zero uses in a 16-minute call is the easiest three points on the scorecard and the cheapest warmth available. Business risks to close out in EMMA today: (1) the destination address is not in the system — 6016 Unice Trail exists, Unice Way is a different street, and he booked the estimate against the zip with the real address only in the notes. That is a wrong-driveway risk on move day and it needs a verified address before dispatch. (2) He committed verbally to moving a washer/dryer to her father/brother's unit in the same complex for roughly ten minutes of added time and quoted no charge for it — confirm that extra stop is logged on the job, because a crew that doesn't know about it will either refuse it or bill it as a surprise. (3) The $70 travel charge is a manual override of the system's $105 tied to an unconfirmed address; once the real address is nailed down that number needs to be re-run and re-communicated before she books, or it becomes a price increase she didn't agree to.
phone_presence_notes: Easy, low-friction, plain-spoken warmth throughout — 'not an issue whatsoever,' 'I'm not gonna kinda screw you over in that sense,' 'thank god' echoed back on the no-stairs relief — and the customer stayed engaged and positive to the end ('Okay, perfect, great' and 'Perfect, thank you so much'), held back from a 5 only by never once using her name and a few rushed run-on stretches.
audio_review_reason: Two scoring-relevant lines are garbled in the transcript and were credited on inference: the minimum reads as 'we have a $20 to our minimum we charge' (almost certainly '2.5 hour minimum') and the No Worries example reads as a 'PS50 TV' with a $30 state payout. Several other stretches run on and mis-transcribe ('get out hair,' 'you still got some Caffe run into my system'), which may indicate a fast delivery worth hearing rather than an ASR artifact — confirm the 2.5-hour minimum was actually stated before this 4/4 clock score stands.
